'''Andrea Grill''' (born 16 January 1975) is an Austrian writer and biologist.

== Biography ==
Andrea Grill studied [[biology]], [[Italian language|Italian]], [[Spanish language|Spanish]], and [[linguistics]] in [[University of Salzburg|Salzburg]], [[Aristotle University of Thessaloniki|Thessaloniki]], and [[Tirana]]. She lived for several years in [[Cagliari]], [[Sardinia]], and received her doctorate in 2003 from the [[University of Amsterdam]] with a dissertation on Sardinian [[Lepidoptera|butterflies]]. Alongside her literary work, she was active in scientific research for many years and [[translates]] from [[Albanian language|Albanian]]. In 2007, she participated in the [[Ingeborg Bachmann Prize]] competition in [[Klagenfurt]]. After periods in [[Amsterdam]], [[Neuchâtel]], Bologna, [[Tirana]], and [[Bern]], she now lives in [[Vienna]]. She has been a fellow at the {{Interlanguage link|Literarisches Colloquium Berlin|de}}, at [[Schloss Wiepersdorf]], and at the German House of NYU in New York.

[[File:GuentherZ_2012-11-23_0355_Buch-Wien-12_Andrea_Grill.jpg|thumb|Andrea Grill in 2012]]
In her novel ''Cherubino'' (2019), inspired by the character of the same name from [[Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart|Mozart]]'s opera ''[[Le nozze di Figaro]]'', Grill deconstructs the contemporary ideal of the self-determined woman. She tells the story of a 39-year-old mezzo-soprano who ''wants to live alone but not in isolation''. Her planned pregnancy, however, jeopardizes her future as a soprano, so she plays a game of hide-and-seek with herself and the world.<ref>Irene Binal: [https://www.deutschlandfunkkultur.de/andrea-grill-cherubino-eine-frau-flieht-vor-ihrer.950.de.html?dram:article_id=454461 Andrea Grill: „Cherubino“: Eine Frau flieht vor ihrer Schwangerschaft], Rezension im Deutschlandfunk Kultur vom 23. Juli 2019, abgerufen am 23. Juli 2019.</ref> ''Cherubino'' was longlisted for the [[German Book Prize]] in 2019.
